triggers: a kernel on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942) risks the '34. CK constants don't transfer without CK access patterns' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942): 34. CK constants don't transfer without CK access patterns

problem.statement: Pitfalls: FlyDSL Flash Attention on MI308X (gfx942) -- 34. CK constants don't transfer without CK access patterns

payload.attempted: CK FMHA uses `VT_STRIDE = BLOCK_N + 8` and `_QK_PREFETCH_DEPTH = 3`. Copying these into the FlyDSL kernel should close the gap.
payload.lesson: Never copy stride/depth/padding constants from a reference kernel without also copying the access pattern that makes those constants optimal. Re-derive from first principles using the actual ds_read pattern of your kernel.

established_fact.mechanism: CK's MFMA tile shape produces different ds_read access patterns than FlyDSL's. CK's depth-3 wins because their kernel doesn't have mask VALU on the critical path competing for the same VALU slots as extra prefetch scheduling. Bank-conflict arithmetic (gcd with bank count) depends on the access pattern, not just the stride constant. Constants that are optimal in one pipeline topology can be counterproductive in another.

payload.observed: VT_STRIDE+8 caused 5x worse bank conflicts and +0.65% regression (trap #1, confirmed on bit-packed mask shape). Prefetch depth 3 caused -0.23% regression vs depth 2.
payload.root_cause: CK's MFMA tile shape produces different ds_read access patterns than FlyDSL's.
